Priya: Quick audit note — onboarding VectorSherpa v1.0.0 -> FP32 baseline looks good, but several PTQ6 variants show a short-query recall@10 regression. Posting minimal repro and immediate hypotheses.
Maya: which short-query bucket? I saw it on short_queries (<=7 tokens) and conversational-snippets.
Jun: can you paste commands you ran?
Maya: sure: compact repro run I used locally:
```bash
# baseline
eval_embeddings --model=vector_sherpa:fp32 --slice=short_queries --metric=recall@10 --index=faiss_hnsw > baseline.out
# per-tensor ptq6 (default backend)
eval_embeddings --model=vector_sherpa:ptq6.pt --slice=short_queries --metric=recall@10 --index=faiss_hnsw > ptq_pt.out
# per-channel emulation
python3 tools/emulate_per_channel.py --model vector_sherpa --bits 6 > ptq_pc.out
```
Sample numbers from quick run:
```
fp32 recall@10: 0.758
ptq6.per-tensor recall@10: 0.688
ptq6.per-channel-emul recall@10: 0.727
QAT-proj-1ep recall@10: 0.745
```
Priya: interesting — per-channel emulation helps, QAT on projection nearly closes the gap. Did you try stochastic rounding during PTQ?
Maya: yes: ptq6.stoch (per-tensor) -> 0.701; ptq6.stoch + per-channel -> 0.734. So stochastic helps but per-channel seems more important.
Rafael: two pointers: 1) short queries are high-sensitivity to small angular perturbations in the projection; measure principal-angle between leading singular vectors pre/post quant. 2) FAISS HNSW params can amplify small ordering changes; check efSearch/efConstruction sensitivity.
Jun: capture recall@100 and MAP too. If recall@100 recovers more, product impact might be acceptable.
Maya: added those to the run. Quick histogram I added in eval to see compression of similarities:
```python
# inside eval
q = normalize(query_emb)
d = normalize(db_emb)
sims = q @ d.T
hist = np.histogram(sims.max(axis=1), bins=50)
```
Observations: ptq6.per-tensor compresses top similarity mass toward 0.5-0.7; fp32 has thicker tail at 0.8-0.95.
Priya: try two targeted mitigations: (A) per-channel only for projection & final linear; (B) tiny QAT (1-2 epochs) on projection using calibration set (2k samples) with dropout off and lr=1e-4.
Maya: queued runs: per-channel(proj+final) + asymmetric 4k calib, stoch rounding toggle, QAT-proj 1epoch (lr 1e-4, 2k calib). Adding PCA-angle & topk-stability fraction metric.
Rafael: also instrument top-k stability: fraction of queries where ptq and fp32 share >=k/2 same ids in top-k. That gives product-relevant signal.
Maya: good idea. Implemented: topk_stability(k=10) = mean(|set(top10_fp32) ∩ set(top10_ptq)| / 10). Will report that.
ci-bot: CI job started: vector_sherpa-ptq-audit (id: rs-2026-12-01-17).
Jun: FYI, try disabling range-fold for the residual branch if present — we had similar tail compression on another model where folding reduced numeric dynamic range.
Maya: ran per-channel(proj+final) + stoch + QAT1ep locally: recall@10: fp32 0.758 -> ptq6(per-channel+stoch+QAT1) 0.747, topk_stability@10 = 0.82, PCA_angle_top3 mean = 0.06 rad.
Priya: that's promising. What about recall@100 and MAP?
Maya: recall@100 fp32 0.902 -> ptq6 mix 0.896 (small delta). MAP drops ~1.1 points.
Rafael: if MAP loss is small and topk_stability >0.8 for short queries, I think we can enable ptq with a short-query fallback to FP32 for critical paths (route queries <=7 tokens to FP32).
Jun: agree, but add canary that wires routing by query token count and compare live A/B on production traffic. Also add metrics: latency delta, token-cost delta, and user-facing error rate.
Maya: will prepare a canary plan and docs. Release note draft: "vector_sherpa/ptq6: supported with per-channel calibration and optional projection QAT; default per-tensor PTQ causes short-query recall degradation — enable per-channel or route short queries to FP32."
ci-bot: run rs-2026-12-01-17 completed; artifacts uploaded s3://redwood-eval/vector_sherpa/rs-2026-12-01-17.json
Priya: thanks — great pipeline. Once we have the full staging numbers, let's schedule a 15-min sync to finalize canary policy.
Maya: will post final numbers in the run artifact and ping. :thumbsup:
